title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) & Vector DBs
description: Explore dense vector embeddings, hybrid search, semantic chunking, and enterprise knowledge grounding.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in enterprise LLM systems?
options: Grounding responses in real-time, external enterprise knowledge
Compressing model weights to run on microcontrollers
Removing the requirement for GPU acceleration entirely
Converting text prompts into binary bytecode

questions.question: Which similarity metric is most commonly used to measure distance between normalized dense vector embeddings?
options: Cosine Similarity
Hamming Distance
Levenshtein Distance
Jaccard Coefficient

questions.question: What is 'Hybrid Search' in modern vector database architectures?
options: Combining dense vector semantic search with sparse keyword search (BM25)
Querying relational SQL databases and NoSQL document stores simultaneously
Executing CPU-based and GPU-based vector quantization in parallel
Running local device inference while streaming cloud completions

questions.question: Why is document chunking strategy crucial for high-precision RAG retrieval?
options: It prevents context window overflow and isolates distinct semantic units
It reduces disk encryption overhead on the vector storage cluster
It eliminates the need for generating vector embeddings
It forces the LLM to output responses only in JSON schema

questions.question: What is the role of a 'Reranker' model in an advanced two-stage RAG pipeline?
options: Scoring and reordering top retrieved document chunks based on cross-attention relevance
Summarizing whole PDF documents into single sentence vectors
Automatically translating non-English prompts before vector lookup
Validating user access tokens against Active Directory groups
